children: The dollar rises sharply after much-awaited U.S. jobs data showed the economy created many more jobs than expected in August. This raises the prospect that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in the coming months, possibly as early as this month. U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 162,000 last month, way above the consensus in a WSJ poll for a much more moderate rise of 53,000. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1%. The DXY dollar index, which measures the dollar's value against a basket of currencies, rose to an intraday high of 99.932, up 0.5% on the day, from around 99.035 beforehand. The euro falls to $1.1583, from around $1.1623 beforehand, LSEG data showed. (jessica.fleetham@wsj.com)
